CHILD CUSTODY

In many matrimonial cases are filed in the Bandra Family Court, the most sensitive issue is child custody.

Parents often ask:

• Who will get custody of the child?
• Will the father get visitation rights?
• Can custody be shared?
• How does the Court decide?

In child custody cases, the Court’s primary consideration is always the welfare of the child and not the ego of the parents.

The Court looks at:

• Age of the child
• Emotional bonding with each parent
• Financial stability of parents 
• Schooling and living arrangements
• Overall welfare and stability

Even if one parent gets custody, the other parent usually gets visitation or access rights unless there are serious reasons.

Every family situation is different. Proper legal guidance at the initial stage helps in protecting both parental rights and the child’s future.

Adv. Khevana Dagli
Child Custody & Divorce Lawyer, Mumbai
Andheri East | Mumbai Central

⚖️ Family Court Cannot Issue Look Out Circular for Maintenance Default – Karnataka HC

Legal Update | Maintenance & Family Law

The Karnataka High Court has recently clarified that a Family Court has no authority to issue a Look Out Circular (LOC) against a husband solely for non-payment of maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.

In this case, a Family Court had directed issuance of an LOC to enforce a maintenance order. The High Court set aside the same, holding that:

✔️ Maintenance proceedings are civil in nature
✔️ Look Out Circulars are meant for criminal cases, not recovery of maintenance
✔️ Enforcement must be done only through lawful remedies such as attachment of property or execution proceedings
✔️ Restricting foreign travel through an LOC violates personal liberty under Article 21

This judgment is important for individuals facing maintenance recovery actions, NRI matrimonial disputes, and travel restrictions arising from family court proceedings.

📍 If you are dealing with maintenance proceedings, domestic violence cases, NRI divorce issues, or family court litigation in Mumbai, it is crucial to understand your legal rights and available remedies.

📞 For legal guidance on maintenance, contested divorce, or family court matters, consult an experienced family and matrimonial lawyer in Mumbai.

Grounds for Divorce under Indian Law 

Divorce in India is not granted merely because a marriage has failed emotionally; it must be based on specific legal grounds recognised under personal laws such as the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Special Marriage Act, 1954, Divorce Act, 1869 (Christian Law), and Muslim personal law.

Common grounds for divorce include adultery, cruelty (mental or physical), desertion, mental disorder or insanity, conversion of religion, incurable diseases (such as leprosy or venereal disease), renunciation of the world, and presumption of death after seven years. Additional grounds like non-resumption of cohabitation or failure to comply with a decree of restitution of conjugal rights are also recognised under certain statutes.

While irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a statutory ground yet, Indian courts—especially the Supreme Court—have invoked it in rare and exceptional cases to do complete justice. Understanding these grounds is crucial for individuals as divorce proceedings are strictly governed by law and judicial interpretation, not social trends or personal opinions.

Law seeks balance between personal liberty, marital sanctity, and justice.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik Sir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Advocate Nitin Satpute is a prominent Mumbai-based criminal lawyer with over 19 years of experience, specializing in criminal and civil law, writ petitions, public interest litigations (PILs), bail, and stay orders.  He has been actively involved in cases concerning human rights and civil rights, often representing marginalized individuals and standing against discrimination.

One of his notable cases includes representing actress Tanushree Dutta in her sexual harassment allegations , a case that significantly contributed to India's #MeToo movement. Satpute's legal actions in this matter brought widespread attention to issues of workplace harassment in the Indian film industry.

In addition to his legal practice, Satpute has served as a Special Public Prosecutor and Special Counsel in cases related to atrocities against Dalits, working under provisions of The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. His commitment to social justice is evident through his active participation in cases that address systemic discrimination and protect the rights of vulnerable communities.

Advocate Nitin Satpute continues to be recognized for his dedication to upholding human and civil rights, providing legal assistance to the common man, and challenging discriminatory practices through his legal endeavors.
